title: Dispatch disruption and access constraints
source_story: User-provided fictional owner stories in this conversation; opening narrative below is a faithful condensed adaptation, not a verbatim transcript.
business_context: 22 staff; 15 field technicians covering a city and surrounding towns.
owner_narrative: Our dispatcher plans tomorrow in a spreadsheet, but urgent morning calls dismantle the route. The nearest worker may lack the skill, part or customer authorization. We redirected someone to a school whose key holder was absent, losing both the urgent visit and the original slot.

diagnostic_interview.question: What makes a job urgent?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: We often accept the caller’s wording without checking affected users or available workarounds.
diagnostic_interview.diagnostic_value: Separates business impact from vocal customer pressure.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: If all jobs are feasible but demand exceeds available hours, a better schedule cannot create capacity; measure backlog and service obligations.

diagnostic_interview.question: Is access confirmed before travel?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: A school contact was not asked whether the room would be available.

evidence.description: A simulated route log shows an avoidable arrival outside the access window.
A simulated assignment review finds the required part in a different van.
Simulated call notes record urgency without impact.

diagnoses.hypothesis: Replanning occurs without explicit feasibility constraints or acknowledged commitments.
diagnoses.counterhypothesis: If all jobs are feasible but demand exceeds available hours, a better schedule cannot create capacity; measure backlog and service obligations.
diagnoses.confidence_policy: Qualitative case-world support only; requires fresh customer evidence before reuse.

interventions.process_first: Collect impact, access window and required skills before replanning; freeze a near-term travel window unless the dispatcher explicitly overrides it.
interventions.deterministic_and_assisted_automation: Rank feasible assignments; display travel, skills, stock and access tradeoffs; issue versioned schedule changes requiring acknowledgement.
interventions.rejected_default: Do not replace the whole service platform or deploy autonomous agents solely because the owner reports inefficiency.
interventions.selection_basis: Choose the least complex intervention addressing the supported handoff failure; compare added administration and integration burden.

requirements.statement: Access and skill constraints take precedence over distance.

requirements.statement: Retain original promised time separately from revised estimates.

acceptance_tests.scenario_and_expected_result: A nearby unqualified worker is not recommended as feasible.
An urgent job outside access hours is flagged for coordination.
A stale acknowledgement cannot confirm a newer schedule.

capability_boundary.proposed_extension: Constraint-aware routing and live stock integration exceed basic skill/availability suggestions.
capability_boundary.pricing: No price assigned; current rate card must not be extended by analogy.

evaluation.primary_metric_definition: Visits completed within agreed windows / scheduled visits; separately report travel minutes, waiting minutes and overdue backlog.
measurement_cautions: Use a stable denominator and comparable operating periods.
Record missingness and changed case mix.
Do not infer staff reductions from reclaimed task minutes.

implementation.baseline: Collect at least one representative operating cycle before rollout; for monthly billing or maintenance include the relevant full cycle. Extend sampling when volumes or seasonality make the sample unrepresentative.
implementation.scope: Start with one consenting customer group and the staff who own its handoffs; include a normal case and each listed exception.
sequence: Reconcile identities and existing obligations with the process owner.
Run the proposed rules in shadow mode; record disagreements and missed exceptions.
Approve a bounded live pilot only after requirements and exceptions have named owners.
Review outcome metrics, added administrative work and failure logs before expanding.
implementation.simulated_resolution: In this fictional case, MILO introduced the process change: Collect impact, access window and required skills before replanning; freeze a near-term travel window unless the dispatcher explicitly overrides it. The team adopted the proposed workflow for the pilot scope. Routine coordination became explicit; unresolved exceptions continued to require a person.
implementation.simulated_lesson: If all jobs are feasible but demand exceeds available hours, a better schedule cannot create capacity; measure backlog and service obligations.
implementation.rollback: Pause automated writes and notifications, retain the event log, export outstanding work and return to a named manual coordinator. Reconcile queued events before resuming to avoid duplicate actions.
implementation.go_no_go: Process owner reviews coverage of acceptance cases, unresolved critical failures, metric direction and staff workload. No fixed performance threshold is claimed without customer agreement.

open_questions: Travel estimates, availability freshness and contractual response definitions require validation.

transfer_rules.applicable_when: Replanning occurs without explicit feasibility constraints or acknowledged commitments.
transfer_rules.do_not_assume: If all jobs are feasible but demand exceeds available hours, a better schedule cannot create capacity; measure backlog and service obligations.
